title: ADR-0007: Credentials & secret management
rationale: Closes foundations-review C2 / seed dagmar-4c9f. Per-Project K8s namespace = trust boundary; 3 typed secret classes (vcs/os-eco/llm) as native Secrets; External Secrets Operator = source-of-truth with native Secret as runtime contract (baseline pre-ESO: controller-managed); encryption-at-rest required; injection Project->Sandbox->dag.Env() least-privilege per-Run; merge stays controller-level (ADR-0006), secrets never in prompts (ADR-0005). Deferred to impl: RBAC/SA-per-Project, short-lived tokens, rotation cadence, ESO backend.

name: Hermetic k3s-in-Dagger bringup (cbb8 spike)
description: Proven recipe to bring up an isolated k3s cluster inside the Dagger engine (dogfood path for dagmar). k := dag.K3S(cluster); k.Server().Start(ctx); then a GO-LEVEL retry loop calling k.Kubectl(get nodes -o wide).Stdout(ctx) until err==nil with a 3s sleep, because k3s writes the kubeconfig before the API serves (readiness race). Returns the node table. Validated on Docker Desktop/WSL2: k3s v1.34.1, nested privileges/cgroup v2 OK, 10-16s cold start. Anti-patterns in the failure record.

Passing shell-loop args to the k3s Kubectl() helper (e.g. k.Kubectl(get nodes ... && exit 0 || loop).Stdout(ctx)) returns an EMPTY string with NO error even though kubectl succeeded — the helper runs sh -c (kubectl + args) and complex control flow breaks .Stdout capture. (Earlier also claimed direct alpine/kubectl containers could not reach the API — DISPROVED by mx-b8452d: alpine/helm reaches the k3s API fine; that earlier failure was the non-existent alpine/kubectl:1.34 image tag, not connectivity.)
resolution: Use the k3s module Kubectl() helper with SIMPLE args (no shell loop), wrapped in a GO-LEVEL retry for API readiness. Direct alpine/helm + k.Config() containers DO reach the k3s API (validated, mx-b8452d) — just use valid image tags.

name: Deploy Dagger engine nested in k3s-in-Dagger (cbb8 — nesting VALIDATED)
description: Recipe: k:=dag.K3S(cluster); k.Server().Start(ctx); waitForAPI (Go-retry of k.Kubectl get nodes, because k3s writes kubeconfig before the API serves); then an alpine/helm:3.14.0 container with k.Config() runs: helm upgrade --install --create-namespace -n dagmar --set image.tag=v0.21.8 --set privileged=true --wait --timeout 5m dagger oci://registry.dagger.io/dagger-helm; then EXPLICIT kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod -l name=dagger-dagger-helm-engine (helm --wait on a DaemonSet returns BEFORE the pod is fully Ready). RESULT validated 2026-08-01 on Docker Desktop/WSL2: engine pod 1/1 Running Ready, 0 restarts, age ~3m — a Dagger engine runs nested (privileged DaemonSet in k3s in Dagger). Confirms Hybrid-C in-cluster engine feasibility for ADR-0008. IMPORTANT correction: the alpine/helm direct container reached the k3s API fine, so the earlier failure record claim that direct containers cannot reach the API was WRONG — that earlier failure was the bad alpine/kubectl:1.34 image tag, not connectivity.

title: cbb8 tenancy direction: singleton engine + per-project cache isolation
rationale: User direction (2026-08-01): a SINGLE Dagger engine serves all Projects (one engine pod, one shared hostPath cache store — observed in the dagger-helm DaemonSet manifest at /var/lib/dagger-* and /run/dagger-*). Cross-Project CACHE isolation is achieved by per-project CACHE VOLUME NAMES (Dagger isolates cache by volume name), not by per-project namespaces. Namespaces are optional (defense-in-depth: blast-radius, NetworkPolicy, ResourceQuota); user stays open to multi-namespace IF it brings a decisive advantage, using a common prefix dagmar-<project> for traceability. Credential-to-LLM isolation is a Sandbox/encapsulation property (tokens injected transiently by controller/engine, never in the LLM-reachable env), NOT a namespace property — this sharpens ADR-0007 rationale without changing its storage/scoping decision. Still to validate empirically: (a) singleton engine serves a client via kube-pod:// (Research Q3), (b) cache isolation by volume name (Q1).

description: cbb8 spike: the nested Dagger engine (privileged DaemonSet, registry.dagger.io/engine:v0.21.8, via helm oci://registry.dagger.io/dagger-helm, in k3s-in-Docker-Desktop/WSL2) does NOT reliably reach Ready. helm install always succeeds, but the engine pod rollout/Ready condition TIMES OUT (kubectl rollout status --timeout=300s) on most attempts; observed 1/1 Running Ready (0 restarts) exactly once (spike-eng5). k3s itself is reliable; the engine pod is the bottleneck. Likely causes (unconfirmed): engine image pull latency into a fresh k3s per cluster name, privileged-engine boot under triple nesting, or resource pressure on the single nested node.
resolution: Unresolved. Engine-pod readiness reliability must be fixed before the kube-pod:// multi-client (Q3) and cache-isolation (Q1) experiments can run. Candidate fixes: (1) persistent k3s cluster via dagger service up so the engine image is pulled ONCE and reused across runs (the dominant cost is the fresh pull per dagger call); (2) resource/timeout tuning; (3) accept that the spike host (Docker Desktop) differs from production (dedicated runner nodes per ADR-0004) and that prod may not have this problem. Singleton-engine tenancy decision is unaffected.

name: Dagger image cache for nested k3s via KeepState
description: The marcosnils/k3s module wipes /var/lib/rancher/k3s (incl. the containerd image store) on each start by default (keepState=false), so the ~500MB engine image is RE-PULLED every dagger call. Fix: dag.K3S(name, dagger.K3SOpts{KeepState: true}) + a STABLE cluster name across calls -> the Dagger cache volume (k3s_cache_<name>) persists containerd images -> engine image pulled ONCE. Measured 2026-08-01: cold deploy 11.5min, warm/cached deploy 17s. This is Dagger image-cache strategy for nested clusters (cache volumes as persistence). Answer to the owner question.

cbb8 spike: k3s flannel CNI is flaky in the nested environment (k3s-in-Docker-in-Docker-Desktop/WSL2). Pod sandbox creation fails with: plugin type=flannel failed: loadFlannelSubnetEnv failed: open /run/flannel/subnet.env: no such file or directory. The engine pod then fails to get a network sandbox and kube-pod:// exec into it fails. INTERMITTENT: the engine pod reached 1/1 Ready once (spike-eng5) but fails on other runs. keepState=true may worsen it by resuming a stale flannel state. This is separate from the image-cache problem (which KeepState solves).
resolution: Unresolved in the marcosnils/k3s module. Options: (a) disable flannel (--flannel-backend=none) + alternate CNI in the k3s container; (b) pivot to kind for the spike (kindnetd CNI is reliable in Docker, kind cluster persists across dagger calls, kind load docker-image preloads from Docker cache); (c) accept k3s-in-dagger as feasible-but-flaky and consolidate. Recommendation: kind is the pragmatic spike environment; k3s-in-dagger feasibility (one Ready run) is recorded, and production (dedicated runner nodes, ADR-0004) likely avoids the nested-CNI issue.

name: Q3 validated: singleton Dagger engine serves a client pod via kube-pod://
description: Empirically validated 2026-08-01 in a kind cluster (the reliable spike environment, after k3s-in-dagger flannel flakiness). Setup: helm-installed the Dagger engine as a privileged DaemonSet (registry.dagger.io/engine:v0.21.8) in kind; a SEPARATE client pod (alpine + dagger CLI from the GitHub release tarball https://github.com/dagger/dagger/releases/download/v0.21.8/dagger_v0.21.8_linux_amd64.tar.gz + kubectl via apk, with a ServiceAccount dagger-client + Role/RoleBinding granting pods/exec) set _EXPERIMENTAL_DAGGER_RUNNER_HOST=kube-pod://<engine-pod>?namespace=dagmar, built an in-cluster kubeconfig from its SA token, and ran dagger core version. RESULT: connected to the singleton engine (client-version=v0.21.8, server-version=v0.21.8), returned v0.21.8, pod Succeeded. CONCLUSION (Research Q3): a singleton Dagger engine CAN serve a separate client/agent pod via kube-pod://, given the client has a ServiceAccount with pods/exec RBAC on the engine pod. This proves dagmar agent-pod-model feasibility. Manifest: /tmp/q3-client.yaml (SA+Role+RoleBinding+Pod). NOTE: dl.dagger.io install script returns 403 from the pod; use the GitHub release tarball instead. NOTE: the engine image (Wolfi) has dagger but no curl/wget/apk, so the client must be alpine-based.
